learning_outcomes.text: Capacity to solve problems within their area of study.
Capacity for abstraction: capacity to create and use models that reflect real situations.
Capacity to act autonomously.
Capacity for planning and organizing personal work.
Capacity for effective communication (in expression and comprehension) oral and written, with special emphasis on technical documentation writing.

Understanding and mastery of basic concepts of fields and waves and electromagnetism, electric circuit theory, electronic circuits, physical principle of semiconductors and logic families, electronic and photonic devices, and their application to solving engineering problems.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts of electric circuit theory and its application to solving engineering problems.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts of electronic circuits, physical principle of semiconductors and logic families and their application to solving engineering problems.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts of electronic and photonic devices and their application to solving engineering problems.
Know the basic elements of a circuit and the equations that govern its operation
Know and understand the basic laws and theorems for circuit resolution
Be able to analyze basic electrical circuits
Know and understand the operation and use of some electrical circuits
Know the basic semiconductor components used in electronic circuits and their behavior as circuit elements
Understand the operating principle of basic semiconductor components
Be able to analyze basic circuits with semiconductor components
Know some basic application circuits and understand their operation
Be able to use manufacturer's datasheets to obtain information
Know the basic logic families and their main characteristics
Understand the operation of basic logic families, and the possibilities of interconnection
Be able to use basic semiconductor components in some common applications
Know the main combinational and sequential electronic devices
Understand the operation of the main combinational and sequential electronic devices
Know some application circuits of combinational and sequential electronic devices and understand their operation
Know the basic photonic devices
Understand the operation of basic photonic devices
Know some application circuits of basic photonic devices and understand their operation
Be able to use manufacturer's datasheets for electronic and photonic devices to obtain information
Be able to develop applications that use electronic and photonic devices
Be able to configure and program sequential electronic devices for their correct operation

syllabus_topics: BLOCK I. ELECTRICAL CIRCUITS
Topic 1. Electrical circuits. Passive components and basic laws
Topic 2. Fundamentals of circuit resolution. Theorems
BLOCK II. ELECTRONIC DEVICES
Topic 3. Electronic components. Diodes and transistors
Topic 4. Optoelectronic components. LEDs, displays and photoreceptors
BLOCK III. DIGITAL ELECTRONIC CIRCUITS
Topic 5. Logic families. Electrical characteristics and compatibility. Output types
Topic 6. Combinational electronic circuits. Gates and combinational MSI blocks
Topic 7. Sequential electronic circuits. Sequential MSI blocks and memories.
Topic 8. A/D and D/A converters.
BLOCK IV. MICROCONTROLLERS
Topic 9. Electronic circuits: microcontrollers
Topic 10. Microcontroller applications.
PRACTICES DE LABORATORIO
Practice 1. Circuits and equipment handling: power supplies and multimeters
Practice 2. Electrical circuits and equipment handling: oscilloscopes and function generator
Practice 3. Circuit simulation
Practice 4. Construction and testing of diode circuits
Practice 5. Construction and testing of bipolar transistor circuits
Practice 6. Construction and testing of MOSFET circuits
Practice 7. Construction and testing of A/D and D/A converters
Practice 8. Construction and testing of combinational circuits and logic family compatibility
Practice 9. Construction and testing of sequential circuits.
Practice 10. Microcontrollers. Development system, application development, simulation and debugging.

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment of theory and classroom practices (works/practical exercises, additional practical exercise(s) with final exam)
Final exam of theory and classroom practices (practical exercises)
Continuous assessment of laboratory practices (individual evaluation of each practice)
Continuous assessment of laboratory practices (proficiency test)

assessment_rules: The final grade is obtained by weighting the theory and classroom practices assessment (70%) and laboratory practices (30%). A minimum of 40% of the maximum grade must be obtained in each part to pass the subject. Otherwise, the qualification will be the minimum of 4 and the weighted value obtained. If one part is passed in the ordinary February call and the other is not, the grade of the passed part is kept for extraordinary calls of the same academic year. Students must participate in evaluation activities totaling at least 50% of the final grade; otherwise, they will be marked as 'Not Presented'.
